parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Start with a business constraint
parts.body:
An AI strategy should say which business constraint the company intends to change. Start with the enterprise plan, the operating metrics behind it, and the decisions already competing for capital. If retention is falling among new customers, investigate where the loss occurs before proposing a service assistant. Perhaps onboarding is confusing, perhaps support has long waits, or perhaps the product itself misses expectations. Each diagnosis leads to a different investment.

Write the constraint as a baseline, an affected population, and a target with a date. For example, an insurer may want to shorten the time to resolve routine claims while holding reopened claims and complaints steady. Its business owner owns that result. The CAIO helps determine whether document extraction, retrieval, or a conventional process change is likely to help. NIST's AI RMF asks teams to define business value and the context of use during mapping, then measure the system in that context. A successful model benchmark by itself does not establish that a workflow improved.

Separate the measures you can attribute to a pilot from enterprise outcomes that take longer to move. Draft preparation time can be measured in a small trial; retention may require a larger study with confounding factors. Agree in advance on the comparison group, baseline period, cost of implementation, and countermeasure for harm. If the company has no reliable baseline, pay for measurement before promising an ROI. The constraint, evidence plan, and decision owner should fit on one page.

example.title: A useful strategy starting point
example.body: A regional insurer records a 12-day median resolution time for straightforward property claims and a 9% reopening rate. It proposes testing document summarization with adjuster review against the existing workflow. The numbers are illustrative; a real sponsor would validate them before setting a target.

exercise.title: Write the constraint
exercise.body: Choose one enterprise priority. State the affected customers or employees, baseline, desired change, accountable executive, pilot measure, countermeasure, and date for a stop-or-scale decision. Name a non-AI intervention you will compare.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map business value and context

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Make strategic choices explicit
parts.body:
A strategy concentrates scarce people, data access, and change capacity. State where AI will be used first, which capabilities the company will share, and which work is outside the initial remit. A company with a trusted distribution network might prioritize better advice for staff over a public chatbot. Another might use AI to cut internal handling costs. Both can be sensible, but they need different operating designs and evidence.

Translate the choice into a small set of investment themes tied to company objectives. One theme could be assisted claims handling; another could be knowledge access for advisers. For each, name the work unit, proposed intervention, measured benefit, major dependency, risk, and executive sponsor. Specify the guardrails that would change the economics, such as a requirement for a human reviewer or restricted use of personal data. Include the cost of integration, supervision, model use, and ongoing evaluation rather than pricing only the API calls.

Consider geographical reach while setting the scope. A service used in the EU may process personal data under GDPR principles such as purpose limitation and data minimisation. In Canada, privacy requirements depend on the sector and jurisdiction; PIPEDA assigns accountability for personal information transferred to a processor where it applies. These obligations can alter the design and sequencing. Have privacy counsel determine the applicable law rather than treating a single market's checklist as the enterprise strategy.

example.title: Two themes, one constraint
example.body: A Canadian and EU service firm chooses adviser knowledge retrieval and assisted document intake for its first year. It postpones automated customer eligibility decisions because source records vary by region and the decision would need closer legal and operational review.

exercise.title: Draft an investment thesis
exercise.body: For two themes, write one sentence on business value, a plausible first use case, the shared capability required, the named owner, and a reason to defer a nearby idea. Explain how the choices fit within the same capital and change budget.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: context and impact
Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada: PIPEDA accountability

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Connect investments to proof
parts.body:
A strategy needs funding gates. Give discovery a small budget to test whether the problem and data are real. A prototype establishes technical feasibility on representative cases. A pilot tests the workflow with the people who will use it and compares outcomes against the baseline. Scaling requires stable quality, a credible operating cost, usable controls, and a plan for training and support. These stages are internal decision devices, not universal maturity labels.

At each gate, write the evidence that would justify additional spending and the result that would stop the work. Discovery can end because the process is already being fixed without AI. A pilot can stop despite a strong demo because human corrections erase the time saved. The business sponsor should recommend whether the benefit warrants expansion; technology, security, privacy, and risk owners contribute evidence within their mandates. Record dissent and unresolved assumptions instead of averaging them away.

Use a strategy scorecard that includes realized benefit, total run cost, quality on representative work, adoption among eligible users, and material incidents. Compare those measures by theme and by stage so the executive team can move funding. Include a countermeasure for each claimed gain. A faster claims process accompanied by more appeals is not a clean success. NIST's Map, Measure, and Manage functions support this sequence of contextual evaluation and risk response.

example.title: A pilot gate
example.body: The claims pilot receives eight weeks to compare assisted and unassisted cases of similar complexity. The sponsor will consider scaling only if handling time falls and reopened cases do not rise; the team also presents human review time, cost per case, and error patterns. Thresholds are hypothetical and must be set from the organization's baseline.

exercise.title: Set a gate
exercise.body: Choose one investment theme. Specify the budget and length of a pilot, comparison method, two benefit measures, one quality measure, one harm countermeasure, decision owner, and the evidence that would make you stop it.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map, Measure, Manage
NIST AI RMF Playbook: Manage tradeoffs

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Defend the strategy in the executive room
parts.body:
Executives will ask why these themes, why now, and why AI. Answer with the constraint, the alternatives considered, the expected economics, the evidence still missing, and the next decision date. Avoid promising that every department will gain the same benefit. A first year can reasonably focus on two workflows and a reusable platform capability while leaving other opportunities in discovery.

Prepare for the CFO's challenge about cash benefits. Labor minutes saved may create capacity without reducing spend. Model a capacity case separately from a cash case and specify how the business intends to use the released time. The COO will ask who changes the workflow; give the operating sponsor a training and supervision budget. The CISO and privacy officer will ask what data leaves the boundary and who can stop a release. Bring a diagram and name the control owners.

Close with a decision request: funding for which stage, approved use and population, owner, constraints, measured gate, and review date. A one-page strategy is useful when it leads to a real allocation or stop decision. If two executives disagree about the objective, resolve that before debating model vendors. Strategy should remain revisable as evidence arrives, with the reason for each change recorded.

example.title: A board-ready request
example.body: Approve a limited assisted claims pilot in two regions, funded from the service transformation budget. The claims executive owns handling time and appeals. The CAIO owns the evaluation standard and reports results after eight weeks. Privacy and security reviews precede use of customer records. All figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Make the case aloud
exercise.body: Write a six-sentence investment brief for a CFO, COO, and risk committee. Include objective, intervention, alternative, cost categories, stop condition, and decision sought. Ask a colleague to identify any unstated owner or unsupported benefit.
